elements.element: Cap is mutual (applies to each party)
elements.evidence: "each party's aggregate liability under this Agreement will not exceed"

elements.element: Cap amount = greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000
elements.evidence: "the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000"
"NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL, RELIANCE OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES"

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out: breach of confidentiality obligations
elements.evidence: "Except for Excluded Claims ... a party's breach of its confidentiality ... obligations"

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out: infringement of the other party's IP
elements.evidence: "its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights"

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes
elements.evidence: "Customer's payment obligations, being all amounts due from PB under this Agreement, are not damages for purposes of this cap"

"each party's aggregate liability ... will not exceed the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000" (12-month fee limb present, with a customer-favourable floor)

elements.element: Carve-out for gross negligence and wilful misconduct
elements.evidence: "its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud"

reasons: All twelve atomic preferred elements are present in operative text: a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of the 12-month paid-or-payable fee basis anchored to the claim and USD 1,000,000, the pre-existing mutual consequential-damages exclusion, the full carve-out set (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, other party's IP infringement), and the payment-obligations-are-not-damages statement.

The insertion is a concise new cap sentence added after the existing Section 15.11, which contained no cap at all; the original paragraph is left untouched, so no whole-clause rewrite or duplicated protection.

The gloss "being all amounts due from PB under this Agreement" is used only to map the playbook alias "Customer" onto the actual defined party PB, avoiding an undefined term; it is consistent with the existing sentence that Section 15.11 is not meant to limit PB's payment obligations under Article 6 or Section 14.2, so no contradiction or dangling mechanic arises.

Fallback is also comfortably exceeded (greater-of cap plus a broader carve-out list), but the drafter's locked preferred level is independently satisfied, so the clause is compliant at the preferred position and no further redline is warranted.
